title: PRD: Recoverable Structured Emission and Function-Gateway Error Semantics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This PRD defines acceptance criteria and engineering requirements for recoverable structured output when models perform multi-stage function/tool calls in streaming mode. Goal: enable clients to resume and reconcile partially emitted structured frames, avoid duplicate side-effects from function invocations, and provide deterministic error semantics across the function gateway and runtime. Deliverables include API contract updates, SDK resume helpers, telemetry events, operator runbooks, and e2e tests against flaky network and worker preemption scenarios.
out_of_scope: Migration of existing third-party SDKs (we'll provide adapters, not full SDK rewrites).
Changes to model architecture or tokenization behaviors outside the runtime surface.
acceptance_criteria: Envelope anchoring: Every streamed structured emission contains a monotonically increasing frame_id and an opaque resume_token; server must accept resume_token to continue a stream from the last acknowledged frame without re-emitting already-acknowledged frames.

Idempotent function semantics: The function gateway must record invocation receipts and expose an idempotency_token for each function call initiated by a model. Replayed streams that re-send the same invocation must be detected and the gateway must reply with the original result or a distinct 'duplicate-suppressed' response code.

Partial-object reconciliation: When a structured object is emitted in fragments, the runtime must emit stable partial-checkpoints. Clients must be able to request the latest committed checkpoint for an output_id and resume with the next fragment index; tests must validate reconstruction under random stream truncation and reorders.

Failure classification: Define and surface three error classes in the protocol: TRANSIENT (retryable, e.g., worker preempted), PERMANENT (non-retryable, e.g., schema violation), and OPERATIONAL (gateway-side function error with optional retry depending on idempotency). Each frame-level error must include an error_code and suggested client action.

Graceful degrade policy: If the model emits a fragment that fails schema validation mid-stream, the runtime must (a) emit a structured 'validation-error' frame with offsets, (b) optionally attempt a single automatic repair heuristics pass (configurable), and (c) provide a clear fallback that the client can opt into (e.g., switch to non-streaming finalization call).

Observability hooks: Streams must emit telemetry events for FRAME_EMIT, FRAME_ACK, RESUME_ATTEMPT, INVOCATION_RECEIPT, INVOCATION_DUPLICATE_DETECTED, and CHECKPOINT_COMMIT. Each event must include output_id, frame_id, resume_token (when applicable), model_version, route, and latency_ms.

Operator playbook: Include a documented CLI command and Console action that allows ops to force-commit a checkpoint for an output_id, mark an invocation as 'compensated', and inspect invocation receipts for debugging. Tests must validate playbook steps in a staging incident drill.

SDK helpers: Official SDKs must expose a resume_stream(resume_token) primitive that handles the handshake, verifies a server-provided reconciliation manifest, and merges partial objects into a final JSON once the stream completes.

Backpressure and ordering: The runtime must preserve intra-output ordering; when backpressure drops frames, resume must guarantee no frame reordering occurs beyond the last committed checkpoint. Unit and e2e tests must inject artificial reordering to validate invariants.
Telemetry SLOs: For resumed streams, 95th percentile resume latency must be under 150ms for hosted routes under normal load, and resume errors must be <0.1% over a 7-day window (measured per-tenant).
success_metrics: Reduction in customer-facing stream resumption incidents by 80% compared to baseline (past 30 days).
Fewer support tickets labeled 'duplicate-function-execution' by 90% within first month post-release.
Resume success rate >= 99.9% for hosted API calls under normal production load.
Average operator time-to-diagnosis for stream-related incidents reduced from 45 minutes to under 10 minutes.
risks: State explosion: keeping long-lived per-output checkpoints could increase memory and storage costs; mitigation: checkpoint TTL and offload to blob store with lazy loads.
Latency tradeoffs: adding reconciliation handshakes could increase first-byte latency for resumed streams; mitigation: async manifest fetch with optimistic resume and background reconciliation.
Compatibility complexity: older clients without resume support must still be able to consume streams; mitigation: server-default fallbacks and SDK rollout plan.

Edge-case function side-effects: guaranteeing exactly-once semantics for external functions may be infeasible in some partner integrations; mitigation: document at-risk connectors and provide compensation APIs.
notes: Related PMs: see PM-314159 for progressive JSON checkpoints and PM-24680 for earlier tool handoff contracts.
Engineering spike recommended: simulate worker preemption and network partition to validate resume_token designs before full implementation.
